description: The dawn of the Mesozoic Era. The Earth was a single giant landmass called Pangaea, mostly covered in warm, dry deserts. Conifers and ferns began to grow, and the first dinosaurs evolved alongside early mammals.

subperiods.name: Early Triassic
subperiods.description: Life was slowly recovering from the devastating Permian Extinction. The land was dry and hot.

events.title: The Great Recovery
events.desc: Life begins to slowly repopulate the desert landscapes of Pangaea.

events.title: Lystrosaurus Era
events.desc: Shovel-faced Lystrosaurus becomes one of the most common land animals on Earth.

subperiods.name: Middle Triassic
subperiods.description: Temperatures moderated, and early Archosaurs ('Ruling Reptiles') evolved, spliting into crocodilian and dinosaur ancestors.

events.title: First Archosaurs
events.desc: Crocodilian and dinosaur ancestors develop an upright posture for faster speeds.

events.title: Dinosauromorphs
events.desc: Tiny, jumping dinosaur cousins like Marasuchus run through the forests.

subperiods.name: Late Triassic
subperiods.description: The first true dinosaurs evolved! They were small, agile predators. By the end, massive volcanic eruptions began splitting Pangaea.

events.title: First Dinosaurs
events.desc: Small, two-legged runners like Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus appear in South America.

events.title: Triassic Extinction
events.desc: Volcanic eruptions wipe out competitors, opening the stage for dinosaurs to dominate.

description: Pangaea split into two massive continents, Gondwana and Laurasia. The climate turned warm and humid, creating massive tropical jungles. This was the golden age of giant long-necked sauropods and plated stegosaurs.

subperiods.name: Early Jurassic
subperiods.description: Dinosaurs claimed the empty lands after the Triassic extinction, growing rapidly in numbers.

events.title: Dilophosaurus Reigns
events.desc: Fierce double-crested carnivores hunt early plant-eaters across North America.

subperiods.name: Middle Jurassic
subperiods.description: As the oceans widened, moist winds spread inland, feeding dense forests of conifers and cycads.

events.title: Megalosaurus Hunts
events.desc: Megalosaurus becomes one of the first giant meat-eating dinosaurs.

subperiods.name: Late Jurassic
subperiods.description: Gigantic long-necks browsed the high tree canopies, defended by stegosaurs and hunted by fierce Allosaurus.

events.title: Super-Giants Emerge
events.desc: Colossal sauropods like Brachiosaurus, Diplodocus, and Giraffatitan dominate.

events.title: Archaeopteryx Evolves
events.desc: The first bird takes flight, showcasing both dinosaur and bird features.

description: Continents drifted into positions similar to today. The first flowering plants evolved, and dinosaurs developed feathers for warmth, camouflage, and visual displays. The era ended in a catastrophic asteroid impact.

subperiods.name: Early Cretaceous
subperiods.description: A diverse period where feathered dinosaurs thrived in forests and flowering plants began to bloom.

events.title: Feathered Dinos Rise
events.desc: Sinosauropteryx and Microraptor show detailed feather impressions in Chinese lake beds.

events.title: Flowering Plants Bloom
events.desc: Angiosperms evolve, transforming landscapes and attracting early pollinators.

subperiods.name: Late Cretaceous
subperiods.description: The climax of the dinosaur age, featuring specialized horn-faced dinos, armor-plated tanks, and giant tyrannosaurs.

events.title: Horned Herds
events.desc: Triceratops and Styracosaurus develop massive horns and neck frills for defense and display.

events.title: T-Rex Reigns
events.desc: The apex tyrannosaur patrols western North America as a bone-crushing hunter.

events.title: The Asteroid Impact
events.desc: A mountain-sized asteroid strikes Yucatán, Mexico, triggering global cooling and ending the dinosaurs' reign.
